props.title: Better Than Sex

sections.content: Better Than Sex sits within a wave of intimate Australian romantic dramas that emerged in the late 1990s, following two strangers through an intense 3-day affair in Sydney. Like Two Nights Stand (2014) and Before Sunrise (1995), it strips romance down to its essential chemistry between two people. Director Sue Dwyer's raw approach echoes similar intimate Australian films like Praise (1998) and Love and Other Catastrophes (1996), which prioritize authentic character interactions over Hollywood polish.

sections.content: The film's frank approach to sexuality follows a tradition of boundary-pushing Australian cinema that includes Head On (1998) and The Last Days of Chez Nous (1992). What sets Better Than Sex apart is its lighter touch - using humor and playful dialogue to offset its intimate moments. The film's structure, following Cin and Josh's three-day encounter in real-time, creates an pressure-cooker atmosphere similar to Weekend (2011) and Medicine for Melancholy (2008).

David Wenham and Susie Porter's naturalistic performances anchor the film in a distinctly Australian sensibility, avoiding both Hollywood glamour and European art-house pretension. Their chemistry recalls other intimate two-handers like 28 Hotel Rooms (2012) and In the Mood for Love (2000), where confined spaces and limited time create emotional pressure. sections.content: Better Than Sex helped pave the way for more sexually frank romantic dramas like Shortbus (2006) and Blue Valentine (2010). Its influence can be seen in later Australian films like Somersault (2004) and Sleeping Beauty (2011), which similarly explore intimate relationships with unflinching honesty. The film's success demonstrated audience appetite for mature romantic stories that don't shy away from sexuality while maintaining emotional depth.
